submission.natural_language_explanation: Duplicate-token head: past a text's first four tokens it is strong (about 0.25-0.75 of max) only on the second or later copy of a rare word-start piece, such as a capitalised name or code/foreign fragment (' Hart' in '...from Hartlepool won, and the mayor of Hartlepool', ' Ger' in 'Mr. Gerlach ... Mr. Gerlach', 'Pro' in 'samplingProfiler ... samplingProfiler'); first occurrences of any word, and repeats of common lowercase words, function words, numbers and punctuation, stay below about 0.25 of max. Separately, tokens 2-4 of a text can fire on any content word or rare piece (strongest with no ' the' or ' a' before it, e.g. 'Gerda Gilboe', 'We know'), so predict a text inactive only if it opens '<Preposition> the <common noun>' (In the morning, / At the end of) and repeats no rare piece afterwards.

rival_explanations: Broader: a generic duplicate-token head that fires on the second copy of any repeated token, so repeats of common nouns, numbers or punctuation ('the new knife', '1842 ... 1842', '"!!" ... "!!"') are active too.

Position-only: the head fires on the first few tokens of any text whatever they are and is silent later, so a repeated rare name deep in prose ('the mayor of Hartlepool' after an earlier Hartlepool) stays inactive.
Narrower: only repeated capitalised proper names fire, so repeated lowercase rare pieces in code or foreign words ('samplingProfiler', 'ursprünglich') stay inactive.
